en.html:
Kanae"In... out... In... out..."
Kageaki"It seems I caused you unnecessary distress... My apologies."
Kanae"No... Though it was quite a heart-break shot, I must say."
Sayo"My lady, you have lost most spectacularly. In a contest of human impact power, or something of that nature."
Kanae"Yes. A foul in the penalty area, I get a penalty kick, now surely I score—and the third pulls the hidden-ball trick. Runner out, game over. Then the scores come in: I lose two to one on the judges' decision. Something like that."
Sayo"Next time, my lady, you must at least arrange to enter through a wall, in accordance with quantum theory."
Kanae"Living in this world is becoming difficult..."

Occupation Captain Kanae Ootori and her attendant Sayo Nagakura.

Those were my two visitors. They had arrived before waiting could properly become waiting.

en.html:
The succession of clear answers stopped. A gap opened.

Miss Kanae did not look like someone caught out by an unguarded remark. She looked as though she were enjoying the interval, savoring it.

Indeed, no answer was necessary. She had already shown me quite plainly where she and I stood.

Why could I not meet my armor?

————Because I must not be allowed to arm myself.

Why did she fear my being armed?

————Because she and I were enemies.

For some reason, then, conflict had arisen between the Prince and GHQ. When it did, she acted on GHQ's side.

Considering what she had said and done before, and that they had very nearly eliminated her together with me on Enoshima, the reason probably was not mere organizational allegiance. Whatever the reason, that was what had happened.

I was indebted to the Prince. Inevitably, that put us on opposing sides as well.

Her warning about the attack on Kenchoji might seem to contradict this. Not necessarily. Perhaps she had merely intended to gather us together and clear us all away.

Everything could be explained. What remained unclear was why the Prince and GHQ had fallen out.

And one more thing.

Why I was alive now.

Why I was being kept alive. Why I was imprisoned in Yokohama instead of killed.

ja.html:
明答続きの流れがここで途切れて、ぽっかりと間が
空いた。

　香奈枝嬢の表情は、失言を突かれて返答に詰まった
人間のそれではない。
　この間を楽しみ、味わっている、そんな顔だった。

　実際、返答の必要はない。
　彼女は既に明らかにしてみせたのだ。俺と彼女の、
立場関係を。

　劒冑との接触が許されないのは何故か。
　
　――武装させてはならないからだ。

　彼女がどうして俺の武装を危惧するのか。
　
　――彼女と俺とが敵対しているからだ。

　つまり。

　如何なる事情によってか、親王とＧＨＱの間に対立
が生じ。
　そしてその時、彼女はＧＨＱの立場で行動した。

　彼女のこれまでの言動、また江ノ島で俺もろともに
抹殺されかかっていた事を思えば、その理由は単純な
所属問題に帰すものでもないのだろうが……
　いずれにせよそうなった。

　必然、親王の恩を蒙る俺とも対立する。
　これと彼女が建朝寺襲撃を予報したこととは、矛盾
するようで必ずしもそうでない。まとめて一掃する為
にそうしただけなのかもしれないからだ。

　全て説明がつく。
　あとわからないのは……親王とＧＨＱの対立の理由
と。

　もう一つ。
　<ruby>なぜ俺がいま生きているのか<rt>・・・・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　生かされているのか。
　殺されず、横浜に拘禁されているのか。

en.html:
A bell announced four o'clock. Only then did I notice the clock in the room. A fairly fine wall clock, out of place in this small chamber that seemed nothing more than a Western-style prison cell.

I considered the intention of whoever had installed it. Consideration, perhaps: a room without windows, where day could not be told from night, should at least have a decent clock. Or a scheme to emphasize the room's general poverty and distress its occupant.

A kindness dripping with malice, providing the exact time until execution so that the prisoner might properly prepare himself?

Or had someone merely sent the surplus here?

で充分、人間は他者に悪意を向けられる。

　自分が人に好かれやすい性質たちだなどとは酒席の冗談
にも言えない事だ。
　俺への悪意に何の理由もなかったからとて、不思議
がるには値すまい。◆が――
